source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

decisions.choice: to Moses and to Aaron: a speech for the priests as well
decisions.reason: As in 11:1, 13:1 and 14:33, Aaron is addressed with Moses, because the priests must teach the people what is unclean and what is clean (10:10-11). The speech runs to the end of the chapter: verses 2-30 are to be passed on to the people, and verses 31-33 speak again to Moses and Aaron.

source.text: דַּבְּרוּ֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אִ֗ישׁ כִּ֤י יִהְיֶה֙ זָ֣ב מִבְּשָׂר֔וֹ זוֹב֖וֹ טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them, a man, a man, when he is discharging from his flesh, his discharge unclean it [is].

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'Any man, when he has a discharge from his flesh, his discharge is unclean.
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When any man has a discharge from his body, the discharge makes him unclean.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'A man may have a discharge from his body. That discharge makes him unclean.

decisions.choice: a man, a man: any man
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun means "each" or "any" (as in 17:3; 18:6). Verses 2-15 concern a man; verses 19-30 give the matching laws for a woman.

decisions.choice: from his flesh: from his genitals
decisions.reason: "Flesh" is here a modest way of naming the male sexual organ, as it is in Ezekiel 16:26 and 23:20, and for circumcision in Genesis 17:11. The discharge is a flow from the penis, not from a wound or sore elsewhere on the body. In verse 7 "flesh" has its ordinary sense, the man's body, and in verse 19 it is used in the same modest way of a woman.

decisions.choice: discharge: an abnormal flow, a sign of illness
decisions.reason: The verb means to flow or run, and is used of water (Psalm 78:20) and of a land flowing with milk and honey (Exodus 3:8). Here it is a lasting flow that is not semen, which verse 16 treats separately; it is a sickness the man must recover from (verse 13). The text does not name the illness, and a flow of pus or mucus from an infection fits what it describes.

decisions.choice: unclean it is: the discharge is unclean, and makes the man unclean
decisions.reason: The pronoun can refer to the discharge or to the man; either way the discharge is the source of uncleanness, and the man and what he touches are unclean because of it (verses 3-12).

decisions.choice: a discharge from his body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the modesty of the Hebrew with "from his body" rather than naming the organ; the meaning decision says what is meant. Literal keeps "flesh".

source.text: וְזֹ֛את תִּהְיֶ֥ה טֻמְאָת֖וֹ בְּזוֹב֑וֹ רָ֣ר בְּשָׂר֞וֹ אֶת־זוֹב֗וֹ אֽוֹ־הֶחְתִּ֤ים בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ מִזּוֹב֔וֹ טֻמְאָת֖וֹ הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And this will be his uncleanness in his discharge: has run his flesh [with] his discharge, or has been blocked his flesh from his discharge, his uncleanness it [is].

en.L: And this will be his uncleanness in his discharge: [whether] his flesh runs with his discharge or his flesh is blocked from his discharge, it [is] his uncleanness.
en.B: This is the uncleanness his discharge brings: whether his body lets the discharge flow or it is stopped up, either way he is unclean.
en.R: The discharge may keep flowing, or it may be stopped up. Either way, he is unclean.

decisions.choice: runs ... is blocked: whether the discharge flows freely or is held back
decisions.reason: The first verb, found only here, means to flow or drip; the second means to be sealed or stopped. The man is unclean while the illness lasts, even when nothing is flowing at the moment.

decisions.choice: the shorter Hebrew text
alternatives: a longer text that repeats the description and adds "all the days of his body's discharge"
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text, which we follow, is short here. The Septuagint, the Samaritan Pentateuch and a Leviticus scroll from Qumran have a longer form of the verse, which repeats the two cases and says that he is unclean all the days of the discharge. The meaning is the same either way. Reviewers should check the wording of the longer text.

decisions.choice: his body / it
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Balanced says "his body" for "his flesh"; Readable speaks only of the discharge.

source.text: כָּל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכַּ֥ב עָלָ֛יו הַזָּ֖ב יִטְמָ֑א וְכָֽל־הַכְּלִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־יֵשֵׁ֥ב עָלָ֖יו יִטְמָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Every bed on which lies on it the [one] discharging will be unclean, and every article which he sits on it will be unclean.

en.L: Every bed on which the one with the discharge lies will be unclean, and every object on which he sits will be unclean.
en.B: Any bed that the man with the discharge lies on becomes unclean, and so does any object he sits on.
en.R: If the man with the discharge lies on a bed, the bed becomes unclean. Anything he sits on becomes unclean too.

decisions.choice: bed ... article: what bears his weight takes on his uncleanness
decisions.reason: What he lies or sits on becomes unclean in its turn, and passes uncleanness on to anyone who touches it (verses 5-6). The same holds for a woman's bed and seat in verses 20-26.

decisions.choice: article: any object, here something used as a seat
decisions.reason: The word covers any made thing: a tool, a dish, a piece of furniture. With "he sits on" it means a stool, a chair or anything he uses to sit on.

decisions.choice: the man with the discharge
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls him "the one discharging". Balanced and Readable say "the man with the discharge" throughout the chapter.

source.text: וְאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִגַּ֖ע בְּמִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man who touches his bed will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And {{gender:anyone|a man}} who touches his bed will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Whoever touches his bed is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who touches the bed of this man becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: wash his garments and bathe: wash clothes and body
decisions.reason: The first verb is used for washing clothes, the second for washing the body. Touching something that the unclean man has made unclean requires both, as touching the carcass of an unclean animal does when it is carried (11:25, 28).

decisions.choice: unclean until the evening: a lesser uncleanness that ends at sunset
decisions.reason: See 11:24. The uncleanness passed on in this way is lighter than the man's own: it lasts a day, needs no offering, and ends with the washing and the evening.

decisions.choice: anyone / whoever
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "a man" here means any person, man or woman, who touches the bed. Literal gives "anyone" with "a man" as the alternative; Balanced and Readable use "whoever" and "anyone" and the singular "they".

source.text: וְהַיֹּשֵׁב֙ עַֽל־הַכְּלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־יֵשֵׁ֥ב עָלָ֖יו הַזָּ֑ב יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] sitting on the article which sits on it the [one] discharging will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And the one who sits on the object on which the one with the discharge sat will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Whoever sits on anything the man with the discharge has sat on is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who sits where the man with the discharge has sat becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: sits on the article: sitting where he sat passes on the uncleanness
decisions.reason: Not only touching but sitting on his seat makes a person unclean (verse 4); the rule is the same as for touching his bed (verse 5).

source.text: וְהַנֹּגֵ֖עַ בִּבְשַׂ֣ר הַזָּ֑ב יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] touching the flesh of the [one] discharging will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And the one who touches the flesh of the one with the discharge will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who touches the body of the man with the discharge becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: the flesh: his body, any part of it
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" most likely has its ordinary sense: whoever touches the man's body is made unclean. A narrower sense (verse 2) would make the rule hard to break and needless to state, but the word could be read that way.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יָרֹ֛ק הַזָּ֖ב בַּטָּה֑וֹר וְכִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And if spits the [one] discharging on the clean [person], and he will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And if the one with the discharge spits on the clean [person], he will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: When the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: The man with the discharge might spit on someone who is clean. Then that person becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: spits on the clean: the man's spittle passes on his uncleanness
decisions.reason: Fluids from his body carry the uncleanness as his touch does. Spitting on someone was also an insult (Numbers 12:14; Deuteronomy 25:9), but here the law is concerned only with uncleanness.

decisions.choice: that person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he will wash". Balanced and Readable name the person who was spat on, so that the reader does not take it to be the man with the discharge.

source.text: וְכָל־הַמֶּרְכָּ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְכַּ֥ב עָלָ֛יו הַזָּ֖ב יִטְמָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And every saddle which rides on it the [one] discharging will be unclean.

en.L: And every saddle on which the one with the discharge rides will be unclean.
en.B: Any saddle the man with the discharge rides on becomes unclean.
en.R: If the man with the discharge rides on a saddle, it becomes unclean.

decisions.choice: saddle: the seat on a riding animal
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb to ride. It is the seat or blanket on a donkey or a camel, or the seat of a cart (the same word is used of the seat of a carried couch in Song of Songs 3:10). Like the bed and the stool (verse 4), it bears his weight.

source.text: וְכָל־הַנֹּגֵ֗עַ בְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִהְיֶ֣ה תַחְתָּ֔יו יִטְמָ֖א עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וְהַנּוֹשֵׂ֣א אוֹתָ֔ם יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And everyone touching anything that will be under him will be unclean until the evening, and the [one] carrying them will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And everyone who touches anything that was under him will be unclean until the evening, and the one who carries them will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Anyone who touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who touches anything the man has been lying or sitting on will be unclean until evening. Anyone who picks up those things becomes unclean too. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: under him: whatever he has lain or sat on
decisions.reason: The phrase gathers up the bed, the seat and the saddle of verses 4-9.

decisions.choice: touching ... carrying: carrying brings a stronger uncleanness
decisions.reason: Touching such a thing makes a person unclean until evening, without washing (as in verses 19 and 23). Carrying it, which means handling it for longer, also requires washing clothes and bathing, as with the carcasses of 11:24-25.

decisions.choice: lying or sitting on
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "under him" means.

source.text: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִגַּע־בּוֹ֙ הַזָּ֔ב וְיָדָ֖יו לֹא־שָׁטַ֣ף בַּמָּ֑יִם וְכִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And everyone whom touches him the [one] discharging, and his hands not he has rinsed in water, and he will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And everyone whom the one with the discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water, he will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: If the man with the discharge touches someone without first rinsing his hands in water, that person is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: The man with the discharge must rinse his hands with water before he touches anyone. If he does not, the person he touches becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: his hands not rinsed: the man with the discharge has not washed his hands
decisions.reason: "His hands" are the hands of the man with the discharge. Rinsing them first keeps his touch from passing on the uncleanness, which shows that the law limits its spread and does not cut him off from all contact.

decisions.choice: must rinse his hands ... If he does not
decisions.reason: Readable states the rinsing as a rule first and then what happens if it is left undone. It does not add to the law: the verse implies that rinsed hands do not pass on the uncleanness.

source.text: וּכְלִי־חֶ֛רֶשׂ אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּע־בּ֥וֹ הַזָּ֖ב יִשָּׁבֵ֑ר וְכָל־כְּלִי־עֵ֔ץ יִשָּׁטֵ֖ף בַּמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And a vessel of earthenware which touches it the [one] discharging will be broken, and every vessel of wood will be rinsed in water.

en.L: And an earthenware vessel that the one with the discharge touches will be broken, and every wooden vessel will be rinsed in water.
en.B: If the man with the discharge touches a clay pot, it is to be broken; if he touches a wooden container, it is to be rinsed in water.
en.R: If the man with the discharge touches a clay pot, it must be broken. If he touches a wooden bowl or box, it must be rinsed with water.

decisions.choice: clay is broken, wood is rinsed
decisions.reason: Unglazed clay soaks up what touches it and cannot be made clean, so it is broken (6:21; 11:33). Wood can be washed (11:32).

decisions.choice: If he touches ... if he touches
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the condition for the wooden vessel, which the Hebrew leaves to be understood from the first half.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִטְהַ֤ר הַזָּב֙ מִזּוֹב֔וֹ וְסָ֨פַר ל֜וֹ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֛ים לְטָהֳרָת֖וֹ וְכִבֶּ֣ס בְּגָדָ֑יו וְרָחַ֧ץ בְּשָׂר֛וֹ בְּמַ֥יִם חַיִּ֖ים וְטָהֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And when is clean the [one] discharging from his discharge, and he will count for himself seven days for his cleansing, and he will wash his garments and bathe his flesh in living water and he will be clean.

en.L: And when the one with the discharge is clean from his discharge, he will count for himself seven days for his cleansing, and he will wash his garments and bathe his flesh in living water, and he will be clean.
en.B: When the man with the discharge is healed of it, he is to count seven days for his cleansing. Then he is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water, and he will be clean.
en.R: When the man's discharge stops, he must wait seven days to be made clean. Then he must wash his clothes and bathe in fresh water. After that he will be clean.

decisions.choice: is clean from his discharge: the flow has stopped
decisions.reason: The first "clean" means that the illness has ended. The seven days, the washing and the offerings of verses 14-15 then make him ritually clean.

decisions.choice: living water: fresh water from a spring or stream
decisions.reason: See 14:5. Only here in the chapter does the washing call for running water, for the man's own cleansing at the end of his illness.

decisions.choice: his flesh: his body
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" is the whole body that he bathes, as in verse 16.

decisions.choice: is healed of it / stops
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being "clean from his discharge" means, to keep it apart from the ritual cleanness that follows. Literal keeps "clean".

source.text: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֗י יִֽקַּֽח־לוֹ֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֔ים א֥וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֑ה וּבָ֣א׀לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־פֶּ֨תַח֙ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וּנְתָנָ֖ם אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And on the day the eighth he will take for himself two turtledoves or two young ones of a dove and come before Yahweh to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting and give them to the priest.

en.L: And on the eighth day he will take for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and come before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the entrance of the tent of meeting and give them to the priest.
en.B: On the eighth day he is to get two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the entrance of the tent of meeting, where he gives them to the priest.
en.R: On the eighth day he must get two turtledoves or two young pigeons. He must come to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the meeting tent and give the birds to the priest.

decisions.choice: two turtledoves or two young pigeons: the smallest offering
decisions.reason: These birds are the offering of the poor in 5:7 and 12:8. Here they are required of every man, rich or poor, as for the Nazirite who is made unclean (Numbers 6:10).

decisions.choice: before the LORD: at the sanctuary, in his presence
decisions.reason: To come before the LORD is to come to the entrance of the tent of meeting, where God meets his people (1:1-3). Now clean, the man may come there again.

source.text: וְעָשָׂ֤ה אֹתָם֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶחָ֣ד חַטָּ֔את וְהָאֶחָ֖ד עֹלָ֑ה וְכִפֶּ֨ר עָלָ֧יו הַכֹּהֵ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מִזּוֹבֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will offer them the priest, one [as] a sin offering and the one [as] a burnt offering, and will make atonement for him the priest before Yahweh from his discharge.

en.L: And the priest will offer them, one [as] a sin offering and the other [as] a burnt offering, and the priest will make atonement for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his discharge.
en.B: The priest is to offer one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on account of his discharge.
en.R: The priest must offer one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} because of his discharge.

decisions.choice: make atonement for him from his discharge: cleanse him from its uncleanness
decisions.reason: The discharge was an illness, not a sin. The sin offering (4:3) cleanses the uncleanness it brought, and the burnt offering (1:3) restores the man to the worship of God, as for the mother in 12:7-8.

source.text: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּֽי־תֵצֵ֥א מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שִׁכְבַת־זָ֑רַע וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֛יִם אֶת־כָּל־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man when goes out from him a laying of seed, and he will bathe in water all his flesh and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And a man, when an emission of semen goes out from him, will bathe all his flesh in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: If semen comes out of a man, he is to bathe his whole body in water, and he remains unclean until evening.
en.R: Semen may come out of a man's body. When that happens, he must wash his whole body with water. He will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: a laying of seed: an emission of semen
decisions.reason: The phrase joins "seed" with a noun from the verb to lie down, and means the semen that a man releases. It is used again in verses 17, 18 and 32, and of intercourse in 19:20 and Numbers 5:13.

decisions.choice: an emission apart from intercourse: a normal event, a brief uncleanness
decisions.reason: This verse deals with a man alone, as in a release of semen during sleep (Deuteronomy 23:10-11); verse 18 deals with intercourse. Unlike the discharge of verses 2-15, this is a normal part of life and no sin. He bathes, is unclean only until evening, and brings no offering. The uncleanness kept him from holy things for that day (22:4).

source.text: וְכָל־בֶּ֣גֶד וְכָל־ע֔וֹר אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶ֥ה עָלָ֖יו שִׁכְבַת־זָ֑רַע וְכֻבַּ֥ס בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And every garment and every skin which will be on it a laying of seed, and it will be washed in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And every garment and every skin on which there is an emission of semen will be washed in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: If semen gets on any piece of clothing or leather, it is to be washed in water and will stay unclean until evening.
en.R: If semen gets on clothing or on anything made of leather, it must be washed with water. It will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: skin: leather, or a hide used as a covering
decisions.reason: The word means the skin of an animal, and so anything made of leather (as in 13:48). Clothing and leather alike can be washed and made clean.

source.text: וְאִשָּׁ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכַּ֥ב אִ֛ישׁ אֹתָ֖הּ שִׁכְבַת־זָ֑רַע וְרָחֲצ֣וּ בַמַּ֔יִם וְטָמְא֖וּ עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And a woman whom lies a man with her [with] a laying of seed, and they will bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And a woman with whom a man lies [with] an emission of semen, they will bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: When a man lies with a woman and semen is released, both of them are to bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: When a man and a woman sleep together and his semen comes out, they both must take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: a man lies with her with an emission of semen: sexual intercourse
decisions.reason: "Lie with" is the usual way of speaking of sexual intercourse (Genesis 26:10; Leviticus 19:20). The verse speaks of husband and wife; other laws deal with unlawful unions (chapters 18 and 20).

decisions.choice: both bathe and are unclean until evening: intercourse kept apart from holy things
decisions.reason: Marriage and intercourse are not wrong; the law makes them a brief uncleanness, so that sex was kept apart from worship. For the same reason the people kept away from women before God spoke at Sinai (Exodus 19:15), and David's men had to be kept from women to eat the holy bread (1 Samuel 21:5).

decisions.choice: sleep together
decisions.reason: Readable uses "sleep together", the plain modern idiom for sexual intercourse. Balanced keeps "lies with".

source.text: וְאִשָּׁה֙ כִּֽי־תִהְיֶ֣ה זָבָ֔ה דָּ֛ם יִהְיֶ֥ה זֹבָ֖הּ בִּבְשָׂרָ֑הּ שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה בְנִדָּתָ֔הּ וְכָל־הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּ֖הּ יִטְמָ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And a woman when she is discharging, blood is her discharge in her flesh, seven days she will be in her menstrual impurity, and everyone touching her will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And a woman, when she has a discharge [and] her discharge in her flesh is blood, she will be seven days in her menstrual impurity, and everyone who touches her will be unclean until the evening.
en.B: When a woman has a discharge, and what flows from her body is blood, her monthly period keeps her unclean for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
en.R: When a woman has her monthly period, she is unclean for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: a discharge of blood from her flesh: menstruation, the monthly period
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, "flesh" is a modest word, here for the woman's genitals. The verse describes a woman's regular period, which lasts for a set seven days; verse 25 deals with bleeding that is not regular. Like a man's emission of semen (verse 16), it is a normal part of life, and it brings no offering.

decisions.choice: menstrual impurity: the state of a woman during her period
decisions.reason: The noun names menstruation and the uncleanness it brings (12:2, 5; 15:33; 18:19). It is often linked to a root meaning to put away or keep apart, since a woman was kept from holy things during these days. Elsewhere it came to mean anything defiling (Ezra 9:11).

decisions.choice: touching her: a one-day uncleanness
decisions.reason: Anyone who touches the woman is unclean until evening. The text does not say that they must wash, in contrast to touching her bed or seat (verses 21-22); it also does not forbid touching her. Her household could care for her as usual.

decisions.choice: her monthly period
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the period in plain words. Literal keeps "her menstrual impurity", which says that the period is a state of uncleanness.

source.text: וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּשְׁכַּ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בְּנִדָּתָ֖הּ יִטְמָ֑א וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תֵּשֵׁ֥ב עָלָ֖יו יִטְמָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And all that she lies on it in her menstrual impurity will be unclean, and all that she sits on it will be unclean.

en.L: And everything on which she lies in her menstrual impurity will be unclean, and everything on which she sits will be unclean.
en.B: During her period, whatever she lies on and whatever she sits on becomes unclean.
en.R: During her period, anything she lies on or sits on becomes unclean.

decisions.choice: lies on ... sits on: as for the man with a discharge
decisions.reason: The rule matches verse 4 for the man with a discharge.

source.text: וְכָל־הַנֹּגֵ֖עַ בְּמִשְׁכָּבָ֑הּ יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And everyone touching her bed will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And everyone who touches her bed will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Whoever touches her bed is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who touches her bed becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: touching her bed: washing as well as waiting
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, touching the bed requires washing clothes and bathing, which touching the woman herself does not (verse 19).

source.text: וְכָל־הַנֹּגֵ֔עַ בְּכָל־כְּלִ֖י אֲשֶׁר־תֵּשֵׁ֣ב עָלָ֑יו יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And everyone touching any article which she sits on it will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And everyone who touches any object on which she sits will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Whoever touches any object she has sat on is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who touches something she has sat on becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: any article she sits on: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The rule for her seat matches the one for the man's seat in verse 6.

source.text: וְאִ֨ם עַֽל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֜ב ה֗וּא א֧וֹ עַֽל־הַכְּלִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־הִ֥וא יֹשֶֽׁבֶת־עָלָ֖יו בְּנָגְעוֹ־ב֑וֹ יִטְמָ֖א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And if on the bed it [is] or on the article which she [is] sitting on it, when he touches it he will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And if it [is] on the bed or on the object on which she sits, when he touches it, he will be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Even if something is lying on her bed or on the seat she uses, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
en.R: Something may be lying on her bed or on the seat she uses. Anyone who touches that thing will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: it: something lying on her bed or seat
alternatives: the woman's blood on the bed or seat
decisions.reason: "It" has nothing it plainly refers to. Read most simply, it is an object on her bed or seat: touching it makes a person unclean until evening, without washing, a lighter case than touching the bed itself (verses 21-22). Others take "it" to be the bed or seat, which repeats verses 21-22, or the woman herself on them. The Hebrew is unclear.

decisions.choice: whoever / anyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he" is any person who touches it, so Balanced and Readable use inclusive words. Literal keeps "he".

source.text: וְאִ֡ם שָׁכֹב֩ יִשְׁכַּ֨ב אִ֜ישׁ אֹתָ֗הּ וּתְהִ֤י נִדָּתָהּ֙ עָלָ֔יו וְטָמֵ֖א שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וְכָל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ב אֲשֶׁר־יִשְׁכַּ֥ב עָלָ֖יו יִטְמָֽא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed lies a man with her and is her menstrual impurity on him, and he will be unclean seven days, and every bed which he lies on it will be unclean.

en.L: And if a man indeed lies with her and her menstrual impurity is on him, he will be unclean seven days, and every bed on which he lies will be unclean.
en.B: If a man actually lies with her and the impurity of her period gets on him, he will be unclean seven days. Every bed he lies on will also become unclean.
en.R: A man may sleep with a woman during her period, and her blood may get on him. Then he will be unclean for seven days. Any bed he lies on will become unclean too.

decisions.choice: indeed lies with her: has sexual intercourse with her
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: not touching her or sitting where she sat, but intercourse (see verse 18). Her uncleanness then passes to him in full: seven days, like her own, and the power to make his bed unclean.

decisions.choice: her impurity on him: the result of intercourse during her period
decisions.reason: This verse gives the ritual result. Elsewhere such intercourse is forbidden, and if done knowingly is punished with being cut off (18:19; 20:18). The verse may have in view a period that begins unexpectedly, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: her blood
decisions.reason: Readable says "her blood" for "her menstrual impurity", the thing that would get on him.

source.text: וְאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּֽי־יָזוּב֩ ז֨וֹב דָּמָ֜הּ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים בְּלֹא֙ עֶת־נִדָּתָ֔הּ א֥וֹ כִֽי־תָז֖וּב עַל־נִדָּתָ֑הּ כָּל־יְמֵ֞י ז֣וֹב טֻמְאָתָ֗הּ כִּימֵ֧י נִדָּתָ֛הּ תִּהְיֶ֖ה טְמֵאָ֥ה הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And a woman when discharges the discharge of her blood many days not at the time of her menstrual impurity, or when she discharges beyond her menstrual impurity, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness as [the] days of her menstrual impurity she will be; unclean she [is].

en.L: And a woman, when the discharge of her blood flows many days not at the time of her menstrual impurity, or when she has a discharge beyond her menstrual impurity, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness she will be as [in] the days of her menstrual impurity; she [is] unclean.
en.B: A woman may have a flow of blood for many days when it is not the time of her period, or a flow that goes on past her period. All the days of that unclean flow she is to be as she is in the days of her period: she is unclean.
en.R: Sometimes a woman bleeds for many days when it is not the time of her period. Or her bleeding may go on after her period should have ended. As long as she bleeds, she is unclean, just as she is during her period.

decisions.choice: a discharge of her blood many days: bleeding that is not her regular period
decisions.reason: This is the woman's counterpart to the man's discharge in verses 2-15: a lasting flow that is a sign of illness. It may come at the wrong time or carry on past the usual seven days. The woman in Mark 5:25-34, who had bled for twelve years, lived with this law.

decisions.choice: as the days of her menstrual impurity: under the same rules as her period
decisions.reason: While the bleeding lasts, the rules of verses 19-24 apply to her. But because it is an illness, her cleansing at the end follows the man's, with seven days and an offering (verses 28-30).

source.text: כָּל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֞ב אֲשֶׁר־תִּשְׁכַּ֤ב עָלָיו֙ כָּל־יְמֵ֣י זוֹבָ֔הּ כְּמִשְׁכַּ֥ב נִדָּתָ֖הּ יִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֑הּ וְכָֽל־הַכְּלִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּשֵׁ֣ב עָלָ֔יו טָמֵ֣א יִהְיֶ֔ה כְּטֻמְאַ֖ת נִדָּתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Every bed which she lies on it all the days of her discharge, as [the] bed of her menstrual impurity it will be to her, and every article which she sits on it unclean will be as [the] uncleanness of her menstrual impurity.

en.L: Every bed on which she lies all the days of her discharge will be to her as the bed of her menstrual impurity, and every object on which she sits will be unclean, as [in] the uncleanness of her menstrual impurity.
en.B: All the time the flow lasts, any bed she lies on is to be treated like her bed during her period, and any object she sits on becomes unclean, as it would during her period.
en.R: As long as she bleeds, any bed she lies on is unclean, as it is during her period. Anything she sits on is unclean too.

decisions.choice: as the bed of her menstrual impurity: the same rules as in verse 20
decisions.reason: The verse applies verse 20 to the longer flow.

source.text: וְכָל־הַנּוֹגֵ֥עַ בָּ֖ם יִטְמָ֑א וְכִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And everyone touching them will be unclean, and he will wash his garments and bathe in water and will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And everyone who touches them will be unclean, and he will wash his garments and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Whoever touches these things becomes unclean. They are to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening.
en.R: Anyone who touches these things becomes unclean. They must wash their clothes and take a bath. They will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: them: her bed and seat
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to the bed and the seat of verse 26; the rule matches verses 21-22.

source.text: וְאִֽם־טָהֲרָ֖ה מִזּוֹבָ֑הּ וְסָ֥פְרָה לָּ֛הּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים וְאַחַ֥ר תִּטְהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And if she is clean from her discharge, and she will count for herself seven days, and after she will be clean.

en.L: And if she is clean from her discharge, she will count for herself seven days, and after [that] she will be clean.
en.B: Once her flow has stopped, she is to count seven days; then she will be clean.
en.R: When her bleeding stops, she must wait seven days. After that she will be clean.

decisions.choice: is clean from her discharge ... will be clean: the flow stops, then seven days
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, the first "clean" means that the bleeding has ended. Her cleansing follows the man's. The verse does not mention washing, as verse 13 does for him; it may be taken for granted.

decisions.choice: her flow has stopped / her bleeding stops
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, Balanced and Readable say what "clean from her discharge" means.

source.text: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֗י תִּֽקַּֽח־לָהּ֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֔ים א֥וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֑ה וְהֵבִיאָ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And on the day the eighth she will take for herself two turtledoves or two young ones of a dove, and she will bring them to the priest to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And on the eighth day she will take for herself two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: On the eighth day she is to get two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: On the eighth day she must get two turtledoves or two young pigeons. She must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: two turtledoves or two young pigeons: the same offering as the man's
decisions.reason: Her offering is the same as the man's in verse 14.

source.text: וְעָשָׂ֤ה הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֶת־הָאֶחָ֣ד חַטָּ֔את וְאֶת־הָאֶחָ֖ד עֹלָ֑ה וְכִפֶּ֨ר עָלֶ֤יהָ הַכֹּהֵן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מִזּ֖וֹב טֻמְאָתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will offer the priest the one [as] a sin offering and the one [as] a burnt offering, and will make atonement for her the priest before Yahweh from the discharge of her uncleanness.

en.L: And the priest will offer the one [as] a sin offering and the other [as] a burnt offering, and the priest will make atonement for her before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the discharge of her uncleanness.'
en.B: The priest is to offer one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for her before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on account of her unclean flow.'
en.R: The priest must offer one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the woman before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} because of her bleeding.'

decisions.choice: make atonement for her: cleanse her from the uncleanness of her flow
decisions.reason: As in verse 15 and 12:7, the offerings cleanse an uncleanness that was no sin. The words to be passed on to the people end here; verse 31 speaks again to Moses and Aaron.

source.text: וְהִזַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִטֻּמְאָתָ֑ם וְלֹ֤א יָמֻ֨תוּ֙ בְּטֻמְאָתָ֔ם בְּטַמְּאָ֥ם אֶת־מִשְׁכָּנִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will separate [the] sons of Israel from their uncleanness, and not they will die in their uncleanness in their making unclean my tabernacle which [is] in their midst.

en.L: And you will keep the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by making {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} tabernacle that [is] in their midst unclean.
en.B: You must keep the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} apart from their uncleanness, so that it does not bring death on them when they defile {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} tabernacle, which is among them.
en.R: You must keep the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} separate from what makes them unclean. Then they will not die for making {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} tent unclean, the tent that is here among them.

decisions.choice: you will separate: Moses and Aaron, and the priests after them
decisions.reason: "You" is plural. The speech turns from the words for the people (verses 2-30) back to Moses and Aaron (verse 1), who are to see that the people keep these laws. Teaching the difference between clean and unclean is the priests' task (10:10-11).

decisions.choice: separate from their uncleanness: keep them from bringing uncleanness near holy things
decisions.reason: The verb means to set apart or hold back, and is related to the word for a Nazirite, one set apart (Numbers 6:2). The people are not kept away from all uncleanness, which these laws treat as part of life, but from carrying it to the sanctuary. The Septuagint has "make them cautious", as if from a similar verb meaning to warn.

decisions.choice: defile my tabernacle among them: the danger of uncleanness is to God's dwelling
decisions.reason: God's tabernacle, his dwelling, stood in the middle of the camp, because he had chosen to live among his people (Exodus 25:8; 29:45-46). Uncleanness is not sin, but holy and unclean must not meet: when they do, the dwelling is defiled, and those who defile it may die (22:3, 9; Numbers 19:13, 20). This is why these laws are given, and why the sanctuary is cleansed every year from the uncleanness of the people (16:16, 19).

decisions.choice: so that it does not bring death on them
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the uncleanness the cause of death, which is what "die in their uncleanness" means, to avoid echoing a familiar wording.

decisions.choice: my tent ... the tent that is here among them
decisions.reason: Readable calls the tabernacle God's tent (as 17:4 does) and repeats "the tent" to keep the sentence clear.

source.text: זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַזָּ֑ב וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר תֵּצֵ֥א מִמֶּ֛נּוּ שִׁכְבַת־זֶ֖רַע לְטָמְאָה־בָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] law of the [one] discharging, and [of the one] who goes out from him a laying of seed to be unclean by it,

en.L: This [is] the law of the one with a discharge, and of [the one] from whom an emission of semen goes out, so that he is unclean by it,
en.B: These are the instructions for the man with a discharge, for a man whose semen comes out from him and makes him unclean,
en.R: These are the rules for a man who has a discharge. They are also for a man who becomes unclean when his semen comes out.

decisions.choice: this is the law: the closing summary of the chapter
decisions.reason: Verses 32-33 are one sentence that sums up the chapter, in the order of its cases: the man with a discharge (verses 2-15), the emission of semen (verses 16-18), the woman's period (verses 19-24), the long flow of either sex (verses 2-15, 25-30), and the man who lies with a woman in her period (verse 24). Like 7:37, 11:46 and 14:54-57, it names what the laws cover.

source.text: וְהַדָּוָה֙ בְּנִדָּתָ֔הּ וְהַזָּב֙ אֶת־זוֹב֔וֹ לַזָּכָ֖ר וְלַנְּקֵבָ֑ה וּלְאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁכַּ֖ב עִם־טְמֵאָֽה׃פ

en.R: They are for a woman during her monthly period, and for any man or woman who has a discharge. And they are for a man who sleeps with a woman while she is unclean."

decisions.choice: the one who is ill: the woman during her period
decisions.reason: The word means faint or unwell (Lamentations 1:13; 5:17). Here it describes the woman in her period, without calling it a sickness like the long flow of verse 25.

decisions.choice: the one discharging, male and female: both kinds of long flow
decisions.reason: "For the male and for the female" gathers up the man's discharge (verses 2-15) and the woman's long flow (verses 25-30), which the chapter treats alike.

decisions.choice: a man who lies with an unclean woman: the case of verse 24
decisions.reason: The last case is the man of verse 24. With it the summary and the speech of verse 1 end.

decisions.choice: a woman while she is unclean
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "[woman]"; Balanced and Readable name her and make clear that the uncleanness is hers.
